leases.summary: [north-star] float4/float8 I/O with PG shortest round-trip output.
leases.spec: Implement parse_float4/8, format_float4/8, input/output/recv/send per module docs. Shortest digits: take Rust's `format!("{:e}", v)` (shortest round-trip mantissa + exponent) and reformat: fixed notation when -4 <= exp < 15 (float8) / < 6 (float4), else d.ddde+XX with at least two exponent digits. extra_float_digits <= 0: emulate C %.{15+n}g / %.{6+n}g (implement %g formatting: precision P significant digits, scientific when exp < -4 or exp >= P, trailing zeros stripped). Input: implement strtod-compatible parsing by validating the syntax yourself, then `str::parse::<f64>()` (Rust parse is correctly rounded); detect overflow (finite text -> inf) and underflow (nonzero text -> 0). Write unit tests in a #[cfg(test)] mod at the bottom of the file (construct contexts with registry::builtin_env(), IoConfig::default(), context::TestSession::default()); tests are compiled/run centrally later.

leases.spec: Write a self-contained backtracking regex engine implementing PG ARE semantics (see module docs and src/backend/regex/re_syntax.n / docs 9.7.3): parse to an AST, compile to a backtracking matcher over chars with captures, backrefs, lookahead/lookbehind, bracket expressions with [:classes:], escapes, quantifiers incl. {m,n} and non-greedy, anchors, flags (i,n,x,q,b,e...). Implement PG's whole-RE greediness rule (leftmost-longest when the RE is greedy). Bound backtracking with a generous step budget so matching never hangs. Error SQLSTATEs/texts must mirror src/backend/utils/adt/regexp.c exactly: compile errors are 2201B `invalid regular expression: <regerror text>`, execution failures are 2201B `regular expression failed: <regerror text>`; use the budget-exceeded case only on the execution path and confirm its text against the oracle. Then implement all Regex-module procs incl. regexp_replace replacement syntax and the SRFs. See amendment pgarbor-types-01. Implement `lookup(proc)` as a `match proc.prosrc { "name" => Some(FuncImpl::Scalar(fname)), ... _ => None }` (SQL-language builtins have empty prosrc: match `proc.oid` instead) over EVERY proc whose generated row says `module: ImplModule::<X>` (grep crates/pgarbor-types/src/catalog_data/procs.rs); each implementation is a private `fn(&[Datum], &FuncCtx) -> Result<Datum>` (SRFs: `fn(&[Datum], &FuncCtx) -> Result<SetIter>` + FuncImpl::Set). Arguments arrive non-NULL for strict procs (the dispatcher handles strictness); return type variants per the datum.rs mapping table. Keep `unsupported()` for procs you cannot implement (it must stay the only unimplemented call site for them). Write unit tests in a #[cfg(test)] mod at the bottom of the file (construct contexts with registry::builtin_env(), IoConfig::default(), context::TestSession::default()); tests are compiled/run centrally later.
